documents.unit: Information Services & Technology and Teaching & Learning Center
documents.title: Generative AI @ WCU - A Guiding Framework
documents.stance_why: The page calls itself 'a living document, not a university policy' made of 'recommendations', and tells faculty to 'communicate expectations' and to 'select ... their strategy'; it sets no AI rule for students and leaves the decision to instructors, so delegates.
documents.summary: A university-wide framework from IS&T and the Teaching & Learning Center with six recommendations: follow policies, protect data, equity, verify accuracy, be transparent, keep informed. It is explicitly guidance, not policy, and leaves classroom AI rules to faculty.

units.why: Purpose statement: the framework 'is to provide ... guidance on the responsible and ethical uses' of generative AI, setting purpose and scope for the community, so it is an institution-level framework preamble.
units.anchor: guidance on the responsible and ethical uses of generative artificial intelligence

units.why: Scope sentence: recommendations 'apply to all members of the university community, including students, faculty, and staff', defining who the framework covers; chosen P56 (framework scope) rather than P61 because it is about who is covered, not what AI is.
units.anchor: intended to apply to all members of the university community

units.why: States the guidance 'will be periodically reviewed and updated to reflect emerging trends'; a provisional, revisable guidance statement, so P54.
units.anchor: will be periodically reviewed and updated to reflect emerging trends

units.why: The document says it is 'not a university policy' and chose a framework because the policy process 'takes time'; this says there is no formal AI-specific university policy, which is P108.
units.anchor: a living document, not a university policy

units.why: Describes how the framework was made: 'initial outline reviewed by students, faculty, staff, deans, and governance groups' then a 'cross-university task force'; the drafting process, so P84.
units.anchor: A cross-university task force then developed the complete framework.
units.policy: The framework was led by IS&T and TLC, with an initial outline reviewed by students, faculty, staff, deans, and governance groups, and then developed by a cross-university task force.

units.why: Invites feedback at 'aiframework@wcupa.edu' and says the framework 'will evolve'; revisiting the guidance and inviting feedback is P54.
units.anchor: Comments, feedback, and suggested changes can be submitted via

units.why: Defines the scope: 'This framework focuses primarily on generative artificial intelligence', so it sets what the framework covers; a definition and scope statement, P61.
units.anchor: This framework focuses primarily on generative artificial intelligence.

units.why: Definition of AI includes embedded features like 'the grammar and language editor in MS Word', widening what counts as AI; a definition (P61), not an exemption from rules.
units.anchor: features such as the grammar and language editor in MS Word
units.fit_note: Also shows routine embedded features count as AI, but does not exempt them from the rules.

units.why: The framework says AI 'is transforming how we learn, teach, and work by offering powerful tools to create new content, assist with problem-solving, and improve efficiency'; names benefits without a rule, P87.
units.anchor: offering powerful tools to create new content, assist with problem-solving, and improve efficiency

units.why: Says the recommendations let the community 'leverage the potential of AI while maintaining integrity, protecting privacy, and ensuring accountability', a statement of principles for responsible AI use (P56).
units.anchor: leverage the potential of AI while maintaining integrity, protecting privacy

units.why: 'policies will evolve as more information about AI impacts are discovered. Patience is needed' states the policy will change; P54.
units.anchor: policies will evolve as more information about AI impacts are discovered

units.why: 'members of the WCU community should commit to choices that limit our negative impact on the environment and climate' names the environmental cost of generative AI and asks for a commitment, so P53.
units.anchor: Choices to use Generative AI have an environmental impact

units.why: Recommendation 1 says 'faculty, staff, and students are required to follow existing university policies when using generative AI tools'; compliance with existing policy is P77.
units.anchor: required to follow existing university policies when using generative AI tools

units.why: Key recommendation: 'Know and comply with relevant institutional policies before using AI tools for any academic and work-related tasks'; compliance with existing policy, P77.
units.anchor: Know and comply with relevant institutional policies before using AI tools

units.why: Acceptable Use Policy passage says AI should be used 'without compromising the integrity of the University's systems and data'; ties AI use to the existing AUP, so P77.
units.anchor: using these tools ethically and responsibly to support academic and administrative activities

units.why: 'do not input any sensitive data into generative AI tools' is a prohibition on entering sensitive data; it concerns personal and confidential data protection, P50 (not P20, which is about assignments).
units.anchor: do not input any sensitive data into generative AI tools

units.why: Plagiarism standard: 'Do not present someone else's work as your own' applied to AI output, asking users to confirm output 'is not a direct copy'; the closest type is P120 (AI output can cause unintentional plagiarism).
units.anchor: confirm that any AI output you use is not a direct copy of other's work

units.why: Fabrication standard: 'Do not present fabricated or unverified information, results, information, citations'; asks users to verify content including AI output, matching P31.
units.anchor: Do not present fabricated or unverified information, results, information, citations, or other findings.

units.why: Cheating standard: 'using or attempting to use unauthorized materials, information, or study aids in any academic exercise' is listed among the integrity standards AI users must avoid violating; treats unauthorized use as misconduct, P36.
units.anchor: using or attempting to use unauthorized materials, information, or study aids

units.why: 'Generative AI tools can be used ethically and responsibly to assist or enhance content development without compromising or violating academic integrity' is a general permission under the integrity policies; default permit, P02.
units.anchor: can be used ethically and responsibly to assist or enhance content development
units.fit_note: Permission is general and conditional on ethical use and integrity; it is not a welcome or encouragement.

units.why: FERPA rule: 'do not input any student records, grades, class rosters, or other educational information protected by FERPA'; protects personal data, P50.
units.anchor: do not input any student records, grades, class rosters

units.why: Research rule: those conducting research 'should ensure that they do not input into generative AI tools any information collected for specific limited purposes, such as research data'; governs research, P62.
units.anchor: do not input into generative AI tools any information collected for specific limited purposes

units.why: Explains that 'AI systems often record, and store data provided to them' and private data may be 'revealed later'; a fact about tool data practices supporting privacy, P50.
units.anchor: AI systems often record, and store data provided to them.

units.why: 'Entering any personally identifiable information (PII) ... could cause the tool to repeat this information' warns on PII exposure; P50.
units.anchor: could cause the tool to repeat this information

units.why: Extra caution advice 'regarding hiring, admissions, or evaluation of students or employees' is data-protection advice (P50), not a rule keeping humans in decisions about people (P73).
units.anchor: Extra caution should be taken with information regarding hiring, admissions, or evaluation

units.why: 'You can share public data that is already accessible by the public with AI tools' is an explicit permission for public data; a narrow permission within data protection, P50.
units.anchor: You can share public data that is already accessible by the public

units.why: 'Do NOT provide data to AI tools if any part of that data should not be included in future results' is a data-input prohibition; P50.
units.anchor: Do NOT provide data to AI tools if any part of that data

units.why: 'Do NOT share Confidential data or Sensitive data with AI tools unless that sharing has been specifically authorized' is a data prohibition with an authorization exception; P50.
units.anchor: Do NOT share Confidential data or Sensitive data with AI tools

units.why: 'Do NOT put confidential research data into AI tools as it may be considered a public disclosure for the purposes of intellectual property rights' concerns research data; P62 best matches because it is about research data, though it is also a data and IP warning.
units.anchor: Do NOT put confidential research data into AI tools
units.fit_note: Also a data-privacy and IP-disclosure warning (P50/P52).

units.why: States 'Most common AI tools are not compliant with FERPA, HIPAA, and GDPR'; a fact about tool compliance supporting data protection, P50.
units.anchor: Most common AI tools are not compliant with the Family Educational Rights

units.why: 'Intellectual property, copyright and contract law around AI is an evolving area' says copyright and licensing are unsettled; P52.
units.anchor: Intellectual property, copyright and contract law around AI is an evolving area

units.why: 'Do NOT submit other's intellectual property to an AI tool without their permission' prohibits uploading others' IP; P49 covers uploading protected works.
units.anchor: Do NOT submit other's intellectual property to an AI tool without their permission.

units.why: 'It is your responsibility to both know and follow those policies' of journals and publishers on AI use by authors and reviewers: defers to venue rules for scholarship, P62.
units.anchor: Many journals and publishing agencies have specific policies regarding AI use

units.why: 'Do NOT submit student's work to an AI tool without their express permission' protects student copyright; applies to instructors, nearest P49 (uploading protected works).
units.anchor: Do NOT submit student's work to an AI tool without their express permission.
units.fit_note: Addressed to anyone handling student work (faculty); P49 covers students uploading materials.

units.why: 'it is your responsibility to figure out how the tool uses data' and 'The university will not be responsible' for unsanctioned tools: users bear risk of unvetted tools, P114.
units.anchor: The university will not be responsible for users’ negligence with unsanctioned tools.

units.why: Recommendation 3 states 'students who can afford paid versions of generative AI tools have a clear advantage'; names equity of access as a concern, P51.
units.anchor: students who can afford paid versions of generative AI tools have a clear advantage
units.fit_note: States the equity problem but no rule such as not requiring paid tools.

units.why: Recommendation 3: 'Ensure equitable access and outcomes by considering how AI use might impact different groups' asks to address barriers and prevent discriminatory effects, P51.
units.anchor: Ensure equitable access and outcomes by considering how AI use might impact different groups

units.why: 'We recommend supporting the development of information literacy skills to effectively engage with AI' recommends literacy development, closest P70 (AI literacy).
units.anchor: We recommend supporting the development of information literacy skills

units.why: 'Do NOT rely on AI for answers in fields you do not know well' warns that errors go uncaught; accountability for verifying output, P31 (it also touches novices, P42, but the rule is about not relying on unverifiable output).
units.anchor: Do NOT rely on AI for answers in fields you do not know well.
units.fit_note: Also says novices cannot catch AI errors (P42).

units.why: 'Verify any factual statements in AI output ... Always check any factual statement in any final document' requires verifying AI output, P31.
units.anchor: Always check any factual statement in any final document

units.why: 'Do NOT use AI as a kind of information search tool (like Google) if the AI tool ... does not include a list of underlying sources' limits AI search to tools that list sources, and says 'Find and evaluate underlying sources'; nearest P31.
units.anchor: Do NOT use AI as a kind of information search tool
units.fit_note: Specifically restricts AI as a search tool to those that list sources; no type for search restrictions.

units.why: Explains 'AI tools can introduce bias' from training data and that tools reproduce gender and race associations; names bias as a harm, P53.
units.anchor: AI tools can introduce bias.

units.why: 'Confirm all claims with known, verified sources' and be skeptical about identity-based claims: users verify AI output for bias, P31.
units.anchor: Confirm all claims with known, verified sources.

units.why: 'Carefully read any copy or images produced by AI for potential bias' tells users to review output for bias; P31 (verify and critically evaluate).
units.anchor: Carefully read any copy or images produced by AI for potential bias

units.why: 'Use caution when prompting AI, since accidental or implicit bias in prompts may result in biased results' is advice on prompting; P93.
units.anchor: Use caution when prompting AI, since accidental or implicit bias in prompts

units.why: 'you are accountable for all output based on the prompts you enter. As the user, you (and not the tool) will be held responsible' states users own AI output; P29.
units.anchor: you are accountable for all output based on the prompts you enter

units.why: Scenario: a student who submits an AI essay with wrong facts or made-up sources 'presents a lack of rigor that the student is accountable for'; a student accountability example, P29.
units.anchor: a lack of rigor that the student is accountable for

units.why: Scenario: a faculty member who emails AI text with false information 'is responsible'; faculty accountability for AI output, P29.
units.anchor: The faculty member is responsible for sending out false information.

units.why: Scenario: a staff member who posts an offensive AI-made image 'is accountable for the content of their work'; staff accountability, P29.
units.anchor: The staff member is accountable for the content of their work.

units.why: Scenario: an AI image that 'recreates the signature style of a well-known photographer' risks IP appropriation; advice to 'provide their own creative direction' rather than mimic, P52.
units.anchor: provide their own creative direction rather than mimicking an existing artist

units.why: 'would a reasonable person expect to know that AI was used to create this item?' gives a test for when to be transparent; recommends disclosure (P24), with the test noted as a partial fit.
units.anchor: would a reasonable person expect to know that AI was used
units.fit_note: Gives a reasonable-person test for deciding whether to disclose rather than a flat requirement.

units.why: Key recommendation: 'Be transparent about AI usage when it has contributed to your work product to help ... support the use of AI to enhance, not replace original thinking'; a disclosure recommendation, P24.
units.anchor: Be transparent about AI usage when it has contributed to your work product
units.fit_note: Also says AI should enhance, not replace, original thinking (P32).

units.why: Lists why transparency matters: it 'develops and maintains trust and credibility', maintains 'showing your work', protects privacy; a rationale for disclosure, nearest P95 (honesty), not a rule.
units.anchor: develops and maintains trust and credibility for all stakeholders
units.fit_note: Rationale is trust, credibility and the scholarly practice of showing your work, not fairness to other students.

units.why: 'faculty should be transparent about their expectations for AI use in the classroom to prevent students from getting into academic trouble' recommends authorities state expectations; P09.
units.anchor: faculty should be transparent about their expectations for AI use in the classroom
units.fit_note: Recommends transparency about expectations without strictly requiring a syllabus statement.

units.why: Students 'communicate the ways they engage with and use AI tools in support of their learning process and any products they create' describes student transparency; disclosure, P24.
units.anchor: Students communicate the ways they engage with and use AI tools

units.why: 'Students are aware of how and for what purpose AI might be used with their information that is maintained by the institution' says students should be told about institutional AI use of their records; P103.
units.anchor: Students are aware of how and for what purpose AI might be used

units.why: Faculty transparency: 'A clear, easy to understand syllabus statement on if and/or when students may use AI in their coursework' recommends a syllabus statement; P09.
units.anchor: A clear, easy to understand syllabus statement on if and/or when students may use AI

units.why: 'Do faculty indicate where AI was used to generate questions, assist with grading and feedback' asks faculty to be transparent about their own AI use in teaching; P47.
units.anchor: Transparent in how they are using AI to support the work of teaching.

units.why: Research transparency: faculty 'are open about their use of AI in support of research and manuscript development'; research and scholarship, P62.
units.anchor: Faculty are open about their use of AI in support of research and manuscript development.

units.why: Staff should be transparent about how they use AI 'for communication, for monitoring, or for managing support requests'; operational AI use, P76.
units.anchor: transparency on how staff use AI tools and functionality to complete the work of

units.why: 'It is your decision (except where it is a requirement for a course or job) to disclose use of AI' makes disclosure optional unless required; a rule on whether disclosure is mandatory, P24.
units.anchor: It is your decision (except where it is a requirement for a course or
units.fit_note: Makes disclosure the user's choice unless a course or job requires it, the opposite of a blanket requirement.

units.why: 'Share the name of the tool or tools used, when the AI was used, and what the AI was used to do' says what a disclosure includes; P25.
units.anchor: Share the name of the tool or tools used, when the AI was used
units.fit_note: Asks for tool, date and purpose; does not ask for the exact prompt.

units.why: 'If you can link to the record of your use or provide the outputs as an appendix or addendum, do so' recommends attaching records of AI use; P26.
units.anchor: provide the outputs as an appendix or addendum, do so

units.why: 'If required, cite your use of AI' points to formal citation standards; P24 citing AI when required.
units.anchor: If required, cite your use of AI.

units.why: 'Communicate expectations and the reasons behind decisions for transparency' asks faculty to explain the reasons behind their AI rules; P66.
units.anchor: Communicate expectations and the reasons behind decisions for transparency.

units.why: Example: a faculty member 'will use AI to create content for class while prohibiting students' because of credentialed expertise; shows an instructor may set a different rule for students than for themselves and explain why; instructor sets the rule, P04.
units.anchor: they will use AI to create content for class while prohibiting students from using AI
units.fit_note: Example of an instructor-set ban on student AI use with an explanation, plus instructor's own AI use (P66, P47).

units.why: 'There is also an opportunity to co-create these rules with students' recommends co-creating rules; P67.
units.anchor: an opportunity to co-create these rules with students

units.why: 'A faculty member may prohibit AI in the classroom completely' says instructors may set a full ban; instructor-level discretion, P04.
units.anchor: A faculty member may prohibit AI in the classroom completely.

units.why: 'Faculty may articulate that the environmental concerns justify no one using the tools' gives environmental cost as a reason for a ban; P53.
units.anchor: environmental concerns justify no one using the tools

units.why: 'Communicate, where appropriate, encouragement and patience as students have received mixed messages about AI use' asks instructors for a patient tone; P66 (care in wording).
units.anchor: Communicate, where appropriate, encouragement and patience as students have received mixed messages

units.why: 'Avoid blanket statements regarding intent in terms of AI use such as "AI is cheating"' tells faculty how to word rules; P66.
units.anchor: Avoid blanket statements regarding intent in terms of AI use

units.why: 'Avoid making comparison about AI use in other disciplines to justify AI polices' gives advice on how to justify rules; closest P66 (how to word and explain rules).
units.anchor: Avoid making comparison about AI use in other disciplines to justify AI polices or usage.
units.fit_note: Concerns not justifying rules by comparisons with other disciplines; opposite of aligning with discipline norms (P109).

units.why: 'we encourage faculty to select and feel confident in their strategy and communicate that strategy loudly and proudly' leaves strategy to faculty; P04.
units.anchor: we encourage faculty to select and feel confident in their strategy

units.why: 'West Chester University has not yet established a dedicated AI Center' says no AI centre exists; closest P108 (no AI-specific structure).
units.anchor: has not yet established a dedicated AI Center
units.fit_note: States no dedicated AI Center exists; not exactly a statement that no policy exists.

units.why: 'The Teaching & Learning Center (TLC) ... Faculty can work with instructional designers in the TLC to develop strategies' supports faculty in learning about AI; P63.
units.anchor: Faculty can work with instructional designers in the TLC to develop strategies

units.why: Directs readers to TLC resources: 'Generative AI Syllabus Considerations', 'Assessment Strategies' and blog posts; points to further guidance, P115.
units.anchor: collection of generative artificial intelligence (AI) resources to guide faculty

units.why: 'Introduction to Generative Artificial Intelligence module ... available for students to learn what generative AI is' is a student AI-literacy module; P70.
units.anchor: module is available for students to learn what generative AI is

units.why: Key recommendation 'Stay informed about AI best practices by utilizing available training and resources' (Recommendation 6: Keep Informed); P102.
units.anchor: Stay informed about AI best practices by utilizing available training and resources.

units.why: Appendix table gives example acknowledgment wordings such as 'Edited for clarity using Grammarly on 10/12/24', showing how to cite tool, date and use; P25.
units.anchor: Edited for clarity using
units.fit_note: Gives sample acknowledgment templates per type of AI use (brainstorming, outline, editing, images, translation, summary).

documents.title: TLC Sample AI Syllabus Statements 2025
documents.stance_why: The document offers 'optional sample syllabus statements to help you craft your own Generative AI policies' ranging from 'Use with Acknowledgement' to 'No Use', so the center sets no stance itself and lists tiers for instructors to choose.
documents.summary: TLC sample syllabus statements: five generic options plus FYE (use and do-not-use), Nursing and Educational Leadership examples in use at WCU. Instructors adopt or adapt them.

units.why: Intro says the statements are 'optional sample syllabus statements to help you craft your own Generative AI policies'; supplies templates, P110.
units.anchor: optional sample syllabus statements to help you craft your own Generative AI policies

units.why: A menu of options (acknowledgement, permission, editing only, idea generation only, no use) for instructors to choose from names tiers of AI use; P05.
units.anchor: Use with Acknowledgement 2. Use with Permission 3. Use for Editing Only
units.policy: The statements offer five named levels of AI use: Use with Acknowledgement, Use with Permission, Use for Editing Only, Use for Idea Generation Only, and No Use.

units.why: 'Use with Acknowledgement' says AI 'may be used in this course so long as you' acknowledge it; a permit-by-default level with conditions, P02.
units.anchor: tools may be used in this course so long as you

units.why: 'Acknowledge when and how you used them' with 'the name of the tool and a brief description of what you did'; disclosure with tool name, P25.
units.anchor: Include the name of the tool and a brief description of what you did.
units.fit_note: Requires tool name and description only; no prompt or output.

units.why: 'When in doubt, err on the side of acknowledgment' tells students to disclose when unsure; P24.
units.anchor: When in doubt, err on the side of acknowledgment.
units.fit_note: A when-unsure rule that leans to disclosure rather than asking the instructor (P10).

units.why: 'Proper acknowledgment ensures academic integrity and demonstrates understanding of the source and influence of generative AI' explains why to acknowledge; rationale for disclosure, P95.
units.anchor: Proper acknowledgment ensures academic integrity and demonstrates understanding
units.fit_note: Rationale is integrity and showing understanding of AI influence.

units.why: 'Verify the accuracy of AI outputs' is a condition of use; P31.
units.anchor: Verify the accuracy of AI outputs

units.why: 'You are responsible for what you submit under your name, even if you used AI to create part or all of it'; P29.
units.anchor: You are responsible for what you submit under your name

units.why: 'AI tools make mistakes that appear accurate to novices' warns that novices cannot spot AI errors; P42 (novices cannot judge AI output).
units.anchor: Be cautious about using AI answers regarding subjects you do not know well.
units.fit_note: Frames the warning around subjects one does not know well, not only beginner courses.

units.why: 'Don't assume AI tools are using accurate sources. You need to double check that the sources are real'; verify output, P31.
units.anchor: double check that the sources are real

units.why: 'I reserve the right to withhold a grade until I have had a conversation with you' states what happens after suspected unacknowledged use: a talk with the student first, P57.
units.anchor: I reserve the right to withhold a grade until I have had a conversation
units.fit_note: Also makes non-acknowledgment the trigger and withholds the grade as a consequence (P28, P37).

units.why: 'Use with Permission' says AI 'may be used for specific assignments with prior permission'; prior approval, P107.
units.anchor: tools may be used for specific assignments with prior permission

units.why: 'When use is allowed, you are required to provide clear citations or acknowledgment that include the tool name and source'; P25.
units.anchor: you are required to provide clear citations or acknowledgment that include the tool name

units.why: 'For each assignment, I will provide an explanation of the rationale behind allowing or disallowing' says the instructor explains reasons for each assignment; P66.
units.anchor: I will provide an explanation of the rationale behind allowing or disallowing

units.why: 'Failure to acknowledge the use of generative AI tools may be considered a violation of the WCU academic integrity policy'; nondisclosure is the violation, P28.
units.anchor: Failure to acknowledge the use of generative AI tools may be considered a

units.why: 'You are still responsible for what is submitted, no matter how it is created'; P29.
units.anchor: You are still responsible for what is submitted, no matter how it is created.

units.why: 'Use for Editing Only': AI 'may be used throughout the course to improve your original work but cannot be used to do the initial creation'; allows editing support (P91) and bans initial creation; chosen P91 as the permission, with the ban in fit_note.
units.anchor: improve your original work but cannot be used to do the initial creation of
units.fit_note: Also forbids using AI for the initial creation and requires own work first (P19, P90).

units.why: 'You are required to provide the original assignment before any AI improvements are made as an appendix'; submit original draft, P26.
units.anchor: You are required to provide the original assignment before any AI improvements
units.fit_note: Requires submitting the pre-AI draft as evidence of own work.

units.why: 'Failure to provide your original draft may be considered a violation of the WCU academic integrity policy' ties misconduct to the draft requirement; P36.
units.anchor: Failure to provide your original draft may be considered a violation

units.why: 'Use for Idea Generation Only': AI 'only for pre-task activities such as brainstorming, structure creation, and idea generation'; P15.
units.anchor: only for pre-task activities such as brainstorming, structure creation, and idea generation

units.why: 'AI tools cannot be used to create assignments' bans AI producing submitted work; P19.
units.anchor: AI tools cannot be used to create assignments.

units.why: 'Final assignment submissions should show how you developed and refined AI ideas' asks students to show their process; P26 (submit evidence of process).
units.anchor: Final assignment submissions should show how you developed and refined AI ideas.
units.fit_note: Asks to show process in the submission rather than submit transcripts.

units.why: 'Any submitted work may be reviewed for AI-generated content' signals checking of submissions; P40.
units.anchor: Any submitted work may be reviewed for AI-generated content.
units.fit_note: Says work may be reviewed for AI content, without naming a tool.

units.why: 'Submission of AI-generated work for this course will be considered a violation of the WCU academic integrity policy'; P36.
units.anchor: Submission of AI-generated work for this course will be considered a violation

units.why: 'No Use': 'The use of generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools (ChatGPT, Dall-E, etc.) is not permitted'; full ban, P01.
units.anchor: The use of generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools (ChatGPT, Dall-E, etc.) is not permitted.

units.why: '(Explain why for your specific discipline and course context)' tells instructors to explain a ban's reasons; P66.
units.anchor: Explain why for your specific discipline and course context

units.why: FYE 2025 'Use AI Policy' repeats the acknowledgment condition as an in-use example; coded on its own: 'Acknowledge when and how you used them'.
units.anchor: Acknowledge when and how you used them
units.fit_note: Used in First Year Experience courses (an in-use example).

units.why: In the FYE Use policy, 'If we suspect you used Generative AI and you did not acknowledge that use, we reserve the right to withhold a grade'; a talk first, P57.
units.anchor: we reserve the right to withhold a grade until we have had a conversation
units.fit_note: Also withholds the grade as a consequence (P37).

units.why: FYE 'Do NOT Use': 'using them in FYE is counterproductive and defeats the core principles of growing as a learner'; AI shortcuts learning, P41.
units.anchor: using them in FYE is counterproductive and defeats the core principles of growing as

units.why: 'true learning happens when you engage directly with the material, think critically, and express your own ideas'; P41.
units.anchor: true learning happens when you engage directly with the material

units.why: 'Unless explicitly permitted, all work submitted for a grade must be entirely your own' sets a fallback ban; P06 (unless explicitly permitted), also P29.
units.anchor: Unless explicitly permitted, all work submitted for a grade must be entirely your own.
units.fit_note: Also a rule that graded work be one's own (P29).

units.why: 'Submitting work generated by AI tools (such as ChatGPT, GrammarlyGO, or others) without permission is considered a violation of academic integrity'; P36.
units.anchor: without permission is considered a violation of academic integrity

units.why: 'you will receive a written or in-person notification. The assignment ... will not be graded until you follow up with your Breakout professor' describes procedure after suspected misuse; P57.
units.anchor: The assignment in question will not be graded until you follow up
units.fit_note: Student is notified and must follow up; grading is held.

units.why: 'the grade on the assignment will turn to zero after two weeks' states a concrete penalty; P37.
units.anchor: the grade on the assignment will turn to zero after two weeks.

units.why: 'The most rewarding experiences will come from grappling with ideas and communicating them in your own voice' explains the benefit of doing the work yourself; P41.
units.anchor: grappling with ideas and communicating them in your own voice

units.why: Nursing 2024: AI 'may be used for specific assignments with prior permission'; the student 'must discuss with the faculty and include the tools they plan to use'; prior approval, P107.
units.anchor: the student must discuss with the faculty and include the tools they plan to use
units.fit_note: Requires a conversation with the faculty naming the tools.

units.why: Nursing: 'When citing generative AI content please use the APA format'; names a citation format, P25.
units.anchor: When citing generative AI content please use the APA format.
units.fit_note: Names the APA format rather than listing tool, prompt, output.

units.why: Nursing: 'The faculty will provide an explanation of the rationale behind allowing or disallowing'; P66.
units.anchor: The faculty will provide an explanation of the rationale behind allowing or disallowing

units.why: Nursing: 'Failure to acknowledge the use of generative AI tools may be considered a violation'; P28.
units.anchor: Failure to acknowledge the use of generative AI tools may be considered a violation

units.why: Nursing: 'Submitted work may be reviewed for AI-generated content'; P40.
units.anchor: Submitted work may be reviewed for AI- generated content.

units.why: Educational Leadership philosophy: 'we, the department faculty, are engaging in continual conversation about the use of AI'; a commitment to ongoing conversation, P54 (policy kept under discussion).
units.anchor: we are committed to these conversations about the current and emerging technologies
units.fit_note: Commits to continuing conversation about AI among faculty rather than revising a written policy.

documents.summary: A D2L Services page defining generative AI and giving responsible-use points for faculty, staff and students: verify output, protect data, cite AI content, check the course policy, and do not let AI replace skill development.
